turns.assessment: The anomaly is channel-specific and begins between the unchanged S02 inbound monitoring and the first changed downstream monitor at S18. A 6.1 dB channel-power reduction at S18 followed by OSNR degradation at S18, S24, and S17 is the signature of excess attenuation applied to och55 at the S02 ROADM. Unchanged amplifier power and pump telemetry, along with normal monitoring on the other lightpath, argues against a span-wide or amplifier-wide fault.

proposals.rationale: A per-channel WSS attenuation drift at S02 would lower och55 before the S02-S18 line, producing the first observed channel-power loss at S18 and propagated OSNR degradation through S24 to the S17 receiver. It also explains why aggregate amplifier telemetry and the alternate lightpath remain unchanged.
proposals.note: site named; resolved to its node equipment

proposals.rationale: A gain tilt in an amplifier on the S02-to-S18 route could selectively weaken och55 without a conspicuous aggregate-power change, but there is no amplifier telemetry identifying a stage and the boundary at S02 favors its WSS.
Added line loss could cause low power and OSNR, but it should affect all channels and normally alter input power at a downstream amplifier; neither pattern is reported.

clarify.assessment: Choose [0] oms.S10-S02|4. The degraded och55 signal travels S10→S02→S18, and its first observed downstream power loss is at S18 on the line from S02. The S18→S02 degree in [1] is the opposite signal direction and does not explain this propagation.
